title: Investigate and prevent non-deterministic kernel reassignment under peaked arrival patterns
creator: Asha Verma
description: Summary: During a capacity surge test and two production incidents we observed intermittent p99+ tail latency spikes tied to kernel reassignment decisions in the inference scheduler. Unlike prior regressions, this behavior is non-deterministic and surfaces only under high short-lived arrival bursts (peaked arrival patterns). This ticket captures the investigation, immediate mitigations, and follow-up action items to make kernel assignment deterministic and resilient to bursty input patterns.
timeline: 2026-02-18: Staging chaos run with synthetic spike generator reproduced p99 spike on quant-8 models (seq_len 512).
2026-02-19: First production alert (us-west) - several routes saw 2-3x p99 increase for ~6 minutes; autoscale did not trigger because average util remained within target.
2026-02-20: Hotfix rolled out that disabled speculative kernel probing during high QPS; short-term improvement but not full mitigation.
2026-02-22: Deeper profiler capture during synthetic bursts showed frequent reassignment decisions inside the scheduler when worker KV cache state was warm but partially evicted.
2026-03-03: Canary with deterministic affinity window deployed to a subset of workers; observed eliminated p99 spikes across canary traffic.
2026-03-09: Additional telemetry dashboards and tracing links added; action items prioritized and owners assigned.
impact_summary: Multiple customers experienced transient but severe tail latency regressions (p99 up to 2.7x baseline) across inference routes using heterogeneous kernel bundles. The incidents coincided with short bursts of requests (10–20s windows) and affected both hosted and dedicated deployments in one region. No request payload correctness issues were observed; cost impact minimal but SLA risks increased.
root_cause: The scheduler's kernel-selection logic allowed concurrent reassignment decisions in the presence of partially warmed KV caches and short-lived bursty arrivals. Two contributing factors: (1) speculative kernel probing was triggered during mid-burst when kernel ranking heuristics had insufficient samples, leading to thrashing between kernels with different performance profiles; (2) a race between cache-eviction and assignment window expiry caused workers to report inconsistent warmness, further amplifying reassignment churn.
investigation_steps: Captured detailed perf traces (BPF + timers) across affected workers during synthetic bursts.
Instrumented scheduler decision points to log kernel candidate scores, probing triggers, and decision timestamps.
Replayed production traces in a stagerunner harness with controlled KV cache eviction timings.
Compared behavior across model quantization variants (int8/quant-8/float16) to rule out backend kernel correctness.
Validated that autoscaling and worker provisioning were not the primary cause (utilization remained under autoscale thresholds).
short_term_mitigations: Disable speculative kernel probing by default during traffic bursts (feature-flagged).
Introduce a minimum affinity hold window (30s) after a kernel assignment during which reassignment is suppressed unless a safety threshold (severe latency regression) is crossed.
Backfill additional tracing on canary workers for end-to-end validation before broad rollback of the speculative probing change.
Customer communications for affected routes with suggested temporary pinning to stable kernel versions.
long_term_action_items: A1: Rework kernel scoring to include uncertainty estimation (confidence band) and require sustained evidence before switching kernels. Owner: Priya Nandakumar. Estimate: 8 points. Target release: runtime-1.26.

A2: Add deterministic assignment windowing in the scheduler - single authoritative decision per request group with quorum from worker health signals. Owner: Liam Carter. Estimate: 13 points. Target release: runtime-1.26.
A3: KV cache telemetry expansion - expose TTL / eviction probability and fold into assignment score. Owner: Diego Martinez. Estimate: 5 points. Target release: runtime-1.27.

A4: Simulation harness for bursty arrival patterns (stagerunner integration) to validate heuristics before rollout. Owner: SRE team (oncall: Mira Johansson). Estimate: 8 points. Target release: runtime-1.27.

A5: Design a graceful fallback policy that favors the incumbent kernel when latency variance increases during the assignment decision window. Owner: Research/Applied ML (Rajiv Patel). Estimate: 8 points. Target release: runtime-1.28.
A6: Run a cross-region canary + blast radius plan for kernel-ranking changes with explicit rollback triggers. Owner: Platform Ops. Estimate: 3 points. Target release: runtime-1.26-canary.
test_plan: Unit tests for kernel scoring uncertainty and hold-window behavior.
End-to-end replay of production traces under multiple cache-eviction schedules in the stagerunner harness.
Load tests with synthetic microbursts (10s/20s/60s) across regions and model variants.
Canary rollout to <5% of traffic with increased observability and automatic rollback on p99 degradation >1.5x baseline.
rollout_strategy: Step 1: Enable deterministic affinity window on canary workers (5%). Step 2: Monitor p50/p95/p99 over 48 hours and check KV cache signals. Step 3: Gradual ramp to 50% with automatic rollback on SLA regressions. Step 4: Ship scoring/uncertainty changes behind feature flags and ramp similarly.
monitoring_changes: New alert: kernel-reassign-rate > 0.5% of requests over 2m with correlated p99 increase.
Expose KV cache warmness metric per worker and create heatmap on Console for quick triage.
Trace enrichment: attach kernel-score-delta to request traces for slow requests.
